response.reason:
NL1 is descriptive/context establishing the device's role as final execution unit for train braking; it names no state or transition and is marked context. NL2 establishes an initial-entry into the braking state upon receiving a brake signal (owner=root/system, target=BrakingState triggered by event 'brake signal'), an alternative endpoint from the same source to OperationalState guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure, and a return endpoint from BrakingState to InitialState triggered by signal feedback sent. NL3 establishes a further endpoint from BrakingState to BrakeCaliperClampingState upon entering the braking state. All three endpoints from BrakingState (to OperationalState per NL2, to InitialState per NL2, to BrakeCaliperClampingState per NL3) are modeled as alternatives sharing source InitialState/BrakingState per discourse: NL2 sets source=InitialState transitioning to BrakingState (initial_entry), then discourse continues source=BrakingState with alternatives to OperationalState (failure) and back to InitialState (feedback) as two separate outgoing transitions, and NL3 adds a third outgoing transition from BrakingState to BrakeCaliperClampingState. Since "if signal transmission fails" is a conditional alternative to normal progression, and NL3's transition happens "after entering the braking state" (unconditional continuation), these are kept as distinct groups: NL2's group covers BrakingState's transitions under signal-related conditions from the entry sequence, while NL3 states an unconditional continuation transition from BrakingState. I split them into two transition groups sharing source BrakingState, each an independent alternative set, to preserve the exact textual conditions without merging unrelated obligations.</reason>

No additional cardinality, event-consumer, guard-disjointness, action, effect, variable-delta, progress, or termination obligation is independently established by NL1-NL3 beyond what the primary plan already extracts: NL2's conditions (signal transmission fails; signal feedback sent) are already carried as guard/event on the existing transition-group alternatives, and no explicit continuous/repeated activity, explicit termination wording, or explicit cardinality count appears in the supplied numbered NL to justify further contracts.

stage_receipts.reason:
NL1 is descriptive/context establishing the device's role as final execution unit for train braking; it names no state or transition and is marked context. NL2 establishes an initial-entry into the braking state upon receiving a brake signal (owner=root/system, target=BrakingState triggered by event 'brake signal'), an alternative endpoint from the same source to OperationalState guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure, and a return endpoint from BrakingState to InitialState triggered by signal feedback sent. NL3 establishes a further endpoint from BrakingState to BrakeCaliperClampingState upon entering the braking state. All three endpoints from BrakingState (to OperationalState per NL2, to InitialState per NL2, to BrakeCaliperClampingState per NL3) are modeled as alternatives sharing source InitialState/BrakingState per discourse: NL2 sets source=InitialState transitioning to BrakingState (initial_entry), then discourse continues source=BrakingState with alternatives to OperationalState (failure) and back to InitialState (feedback) as two separate outgoing transitions, and NL3 adds a third outgoing transition from BrakingState to BrakeCaliperClampingState. Since "if signal transmission fails" is a conditional alternative to normal progression, and NL3's transition happens "after entering the braking state" (unconditional continuation), these are kept as distinct groups: NL2's group covers BrakingState's transitions under signal-related conditions from the entry sequence, while NL3 states an unconditional continuation transition from BrakingState. I split them into two transition groups sharing source BrakingState, each an independent alternative set, to preserve the exact textual conditions without merging unrelated obligations.</reason>
